questions.question: Which instrument is described as a hand drum used by tribal communities in the hilly areas of Tripura and Meghalaya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dama**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dama** is a traditional **percussion instrument**, specifically a long, narrow **hand drum** widely used by tribal communities in the hilly terrains of **Meghalaya** and **Tripura**.
 
• It is most prominently associated with the **Garo tribe** and serves as a vital cultural element during their major social and religious ceremonies.
 
• The instrument is traditionally crafted from a **hollowed-out wooden log**, usually from the **Gambhar tree** or other local timber, with animal hide (typically goat skin) stretched tightly across the circular ends to produce a resonant sound.
 
• It plays a central role in the **Wangala Festival**, popularly known as the **One Hundred Drums Festival**, which is a harvest celebration dedicated to the Sun God **Saljong**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhak**:

 
 
• A large **barrel-shaped membranophone** predominantly used in **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• It is an essential part of the **Durga Puja** celebrations and is typically played using two thin wooden sticks rather than bare hands.
 
 
 
• **Davandi**:
 
 
• A small, **hourglass-shaped drum** similar to the damaru, commonly found in the folk music traditions of **Maharashtra** and Southern India.
 
• It is often used by wandering folk singers or in specific local rituals to accompany devotional performances.
 
 
 
• **Chyabrung**:
 
 
• The **Chyabrung** is a traditional drum belonging to the **Limbu community** residing in **Sikkim**, **Darjeeling**, and **Nepal**.
 
• It is hung around the neck and played with both hands during the **Chyabrung dance** (Kelang), performed during harvest festivals like **Chasok Tangnam**.

questions.question: The Chota Nagpur Plateau of eastern India is especially known for the abundance of which of the following mineral resources that support the country’s industry?

options.text: Limestone used primarily for cement manufacture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coal and iron ore deposits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chota Nagpur Plateau** is a continental plateau in eastern India, covering much of **Jharkhand** as well as adjacent parts of **Odisha**, **West Bengal**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It is famously known as the **Mineral Heart of India** because it stores a vast variety of minerals, accounting for nearly **40 percent** of the country's total mineral wealth.
 
• The region contains the largest **Gondwana coal** deposits in the country, primarily located in the **Damodar Valley** area including **Jharia**, **Raniganj**, and **Bokaro**, which fuel the nation's thermal power and metallurgical sectors.
 
• Abundant high-grade **iron ore** (Hematite) is found in the **Singhbhum** district of Jharkhand and the **Mayurbhanj-Keonjhar** belt of Odisha, making it the backbone of the **Iron and Steel Industry**.
 
• The availability of these two critical resources in close proximity led to the development of major industrial hubs such as **Jamshedpur (TISCO)**, **Bokaro**, and **Durgapur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mineral Diversity**:

 
 
• The plateau is also the world's leading producer of **Mica**, concentrated in the **Koderma** region, and holds significant **Bauxite** and **Copper** reserves.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options Context**:
 
 
• **Diamond-bearing kimberlite**: These are primarily located in the **Panna** district of **Madhya Pradesh** and parts of the **Raipur** district in Chhattisgarh, not the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
 
• **Petroleum and natural gas**: These fossil fuels are found in sedimentary basins such as **Mumbai High**, **Assam (Digboi)**, and the **Krishna-Godavari** offshore basin.
 
• **Limestone**: While present, it is not the defining industrial mineral of this specific plateau; it is more extensively mined for cement in **Rajasthan**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Andhra Pradesh**.

questions.question: Vice‑President CP Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 30th CII Partnership Summit in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Visakhapatnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **30th edition** of the **CII Partnership Summit** was inaugurated by **CP Radhakrishnan** in the port city of **Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The summit was organized by the **Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)** in partnership with the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, and the **State Government of Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• This milestone **30th edition** serves as a premier platform for **global leaders**, **policymakers**, and **business icons** to discuss **economic growth**, **international trade**, and **investment opportunities**.
 
• The choice of **Visakhapatnam**, often referred to as the **City of Destiny**, highlights its strategic importance as an **industrial hub** and its contribution to India's **maritime trade** and **blue economy**.
 
• The summit focused on themes such as **Sustainable Development**, **Inclusive Growth**, and **Technological Innovation** in a rapidly changing global economic landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Confederation of Indian Industry (CII)**:

 
 
• It is a **non-government**, **not-for-profit**, industry-led organization founded in **1895**.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it works closely with the **Government of India** on policy issues to enhance the efficiency and competitiveness of **Indian Industry**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of the Summit**:
 
 
• The **Partnership Summit** was launched in **1995** to commemorate the **Centenary** of **CII**.
 
• Since its inception, it has emerged as one of the most prominent **international investment summits** in India, facilitating high-level **B2B** and **B2G** networking.
 
 
 
• **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**:
 
 
• Operating under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, **DPIIT** is responsible for formulating and implementing **industrial policy** and **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** policy.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in the **Make in India** and **Startup India** initiatives to boost the **manufacturing sector**.

questions.question: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised India’s GDP growth forecast for FY26 to .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, during its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meeting in **December 2024**, released the growth projections for the financial year **2025-26 (FY26)**, pegging the real **GDP growth** at **7.3%**.
 
• The quarterly breakup for the **FY26** growth forecast is as follows: **Q1** at **7.3%**, **Q2** at **7.4%**, **Q3** at **7.2%**, and **Q4** at **7.1%**, indicating a steady economic momentum throughout the year.
 
• The projection is supported by factors such as resilient **investment activity**, improving **rural demand**, and a sustained uptick in the **services sector**, which continues to be a primary driver of the Indian economy.
 
• RBI Governor **Shaktikanta Das** noted that while global headwinds persist, the domestic structural reforms and strong **corporate balance sheets** provide a cushion for achieving this **7.3%** growth target.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**

 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory body under the **RBI Act, 1934**, responsible for determining the **Policy Repo Rate** to achieve the inflation target.
 
• It consists of **six members**, including three from the **RBI** and three external members appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
• The primary objective is to maintain **price stability** while keeping the objective of **economic growth** in focus, targeting an inflation rate of **4%** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%**.
 
 
 
• **GDP Growth Metrics:**
 
 
• **Real GDP** is calculated using constant prices (base year **2011-12** in India) to account for **inflation**, providing a clearer picture of actual economic expansion.
 
• The **Gross Value Added (GVA)** is another critical metric used by the **RBI** to analyze supply-side performance across sectors like **Agriculture**, **Industry**, and **Services**.
 
• Sustained **Capital Expenditure (Capex)** by the Central Government is a key catalyst mentioned by the **RBI** for achieving high growth rates in **FY26**.

questions.question: Which among the following slogans was popularised by Bal Gangadhar Tilak?

options.text: Liberty is our dream and we must attain it
Give me blood and I will give you freedom
Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
Freedom is our goal and we shall achieve it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, also known as **Lokmanya Tilak**, popularised the iconic slogan **Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it** to ignite the spirit of independence among Indians.
 
• The slogan was prominently used during the **Home Rule Movement** around **1916**, signaling a shift in the **Indian National Movement** toward a more assertive demand for self-governance.
 
• Tilak was a key leader of the **Extremist** faction within the **Indian National Congress**, advocating for **Swaraj** (Self-Rule) rather than mere administrative reforms.
 
• By using this slogan, he successfully mobilised the masses, transforming the freedom struggle from an elite-driven movement into a **mass movement**.
 
• He was famously described by British colonial authorities as the **Father of the Indian Unrest** due to his radical nationalist activities and influential writings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Give me blood and I will give you freedom**:

 
 
• This slogan was given by **Subhash Chandra Bose**, also known as **Netaji**.
 
• It was used to recruit and inspire soldiers of the **Indian National Army (INA)** or **Azad Hind Fauj** to fight against the **British Empire** during **World War II**.
 
 
 
• **Contributions of Bal Gangadhar Tilak**:
 
 
• He started two influential newspapers: **Kesari** in **Marathi** and **The Mahratta** in **English**.
 
• Tilak introduced public celebrations of **Ganesh Chaturthi** and **Shivaji Jayanti** to build national unity and cultural pride.
 
• He authored several books, including **Gita Rahasya**, which he wrote during his imprisonment in **Mandalay Jail**, and **The Arctic Home in the Vedas**.
 
• He was a founding member of the **Deccan Education Society** and the **Fergusson College** in **Pune**.

questions.question: Which country has requested WTO dispute consultations with India regarding certain Indian measures in the automotive and renewable energy sectors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **September 11, 2024**, **China** formally requested **World Trade Organization (WTO)** dispute consultations with **India**.
 
• The dispute centers on **Indian measures** affecting the **automotive** and **renewable energy** sectors, specifically targeting certain **import duties** and **subsidies** provided by the Indian government.
 
• **China** claims that these measures are inconsistent with various provisions of the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) 1944** and the **Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures (SCM Agreement)**.
 
• The request specifically highlights concerns regarding **local content requirements** and financial incentives that **China** argues disadvantage foreign products in the Indian market.
 
• This action marks a significant escalation in trade tensions between the two neighbors, following India's increased scrutiny of **Chinese investments** and imports under its **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **WTO Dispute Settlement Process**:

 
 
• **Consultations**: The first stage where parties attempt to resolve differences within **60 days**.
 
• **Panel Establishment**: If consultations fail, the complaining nation can request a **Dispute Settlement Panel** to adjudicate the matter.
 
 
 
• **India's Strategic Sectors**:
 
 
• The **Automotive sector** in India is supported by the **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme** for **Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC)** and **Auto Components**.
 
• In **Renewable Energy**, India has implemented the **Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM)** to boost domestic manufacturing of **Solar Photovoltaic (PV) modules**.
 
 
 
• **USA and Brazil**:
 
 
• While the **United States** and **Brazil** have had past trade disagreements with India regarding **sugar subsidies** and **poultry imports**, they are not the initiators of this specific 2024 automotive and renewable energy complaint.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the ‘Aapki Punji Aapka Adhikar’ campaign, launched in 2025?

options.text: Digitizing all personal banking accounts under the Jan Dhan and UPI framework for transparency
Facilitating speedy settlement and rightful return of unclaimed financial assets to legitimate claimants
Encouraging citizens to invest in long-term pension and insurance instruments for wealth creation
Expanding micro-credit access for small businesses and self-help groups across rural districts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Facilitating speedy settlement and rightful return of unclaimed financial assets to legitimate claimants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aapki Punji Aapka Adhikar** campaign was launched in **2025** as a nationwide mission to address the growing volume of **unclaimed financial assets** across the country.
 
• Its primary objective is to create a **centralized and simplified framework** that allows **legal heirs** and **legitimate owners** to identify and recover funds that have been lying dormant.
 
• The initiative focuses on various asset classes, including **bank deposits**, **matured insurance policies**, **unpaid dividends**, and **matured debentures** that have not been claimed for years.
 
• The campaign employs **technological integration** to facilitate **speedy settlements**, reducing the bureaucratic hurdles and lengthy paperwork previously associated with **legacy claims**.
 
• It aims to enhance **financial justice** by ensuring that **household savings** are returned to the families or individuals who are the rightful beneficiaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unclaimed Deposits and Assets**:

 
 
• In the **banking sector**, accounts are classified as **unclaimed** if they remain **inoperative** or **inactive** for a continuous period of **10 years**.
 
• Such funds are periodically transferred to the **Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund**, which is maintained and monitored by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Support**:
 
 
• The campaign heavily utilizes the **UDGAM (Unclaimed Deposits-Gateway to Access Information)** portal, which acts as a **single window** for citizens to search for their deposits across multiple banks.
 
• Advanced **KYC (Know Your Customer)** verification and **biometric authentication** are used to prevent **fraudulent claims** during the settlement process.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Measures**:
 
 
• Beyond recovery, the campaign emphasizes **financial literacy** by urging account holders to maintain **active nominations**.
 
• It encourages **periodic updates** of contact details and **Aadhaar linking** to ensure that assets do not become **untraceable** in the future.

questions.question: Which of the following dimensions is NOT directly included in the Human Development Index (HDI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human security**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a summary measure of average achievement in key dimensions of human development, developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• It was created by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian economist **Amartya Sen** in **1990** to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing development.
 
• The index is calculated using three specific dimensions: **a long and healthy life**, **being knowledgeable**, and **a decent standard of living**.
 
• **Human security** is a distinct conceptual framework introduced in the **1994 Human Development Report** that addresses freedom from fear and freedom from want, but it is not used as a quantitative variable in the primary **HDI** calculation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A long and healthy life**:

 
 
• This dimension is assessed by the **Life Expectancy at Birth** indicator.
 
• It reflects the overall health status of a population and the effectiveness of the **healthcare system**.
 
 
 
• **Being knowledgeable**:
 
 
• Measured through two indicators: **Mean years of schooling** for adults aged 25 years and older, and **Expected years of schooling** for children of school-entering age.
 
• These metrics provide a holistic view of the **educational attainment** and potential within a country.
 
 
 
• **A decent standard of living**:
 
 
• Measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in international dollars.
 
• This accounts for the differences in the **cost of living** and **inflation** rates across different nations.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Indices**:
 
 
• The UNDP also publishes the **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**, the **Gender Development Index (GDI)**, and the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** to provide a more comprehensive view of social progress.

questions.question: Words 'Integrity', 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by which of the following amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment, 1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act**, passed in **1976**, is historically significant as it remains the only time the **Preamble** of the **Constitution of India** has been amended to date.
 
• This amendment officially inserted three specific terms into the **Preamble**: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**, thereby redefining the nature of the Indian State.
 
• The description of India was transformed from a **Sovereign Democratic Republic** to a **Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic**.
 
• Furthermore, the phrase **unity of the Nation** was amended to read **unity and integrity of the Nation** to emphasize national cohesion.
 
• The amendment was enacted during the **National Emergency** under the administration of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, following the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mini-Constitution**:

 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** is widely known as the **Mini-Constitution** due to the extensive and sweeping changes it introduced across various **Articles** and **Schedules**.
 
• It added **Part IV-A** (Fundamental Duties) and **Part XIV-A** (Administrative Tribunals) to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **24th Amendment, 1971**:
 
 
• This act affirmed the **Parliamentary power** to amend any part of the Constitution, including **Fundamental Rights**, in response to the **Golaknath case**.
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment, 1978**:
 
 
• Introduced by the **Janata Government** to restore democratic safeguards and notably removed the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights, making it a legal right under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **52nd Amendment, 1985**:
 
 
• Introduced the **Anti-Defection Law** by adding the **Tenth Schedule** to the Constitution to curb political instability caused by floor-crossing.

questions.question: Which of the following British Indian government legislation separated for the first time 'provincial budgets' from the 'central budget' and authorised the provincial legislatures to enact their budgets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act of 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• A fundamental shift in the fiscal administration occurred when this Act separated **Provincial budgets** from the **Central budget** for the first time in **British Indian** history.
